analysis:
The supplied change is documentation only (docs/operations/provider-release.md). Changed ranges are base 174, 497-508, 510-511, 517, 521, 530-532, and the matching head ranges. The patch excerpt is truncated after the start of the new dev-branch lane description. The lane moves from a push trigger to a 6-hour schedule (`23 */6 * * *`) plus manual workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev, with a `gate` job on ubuntu-24.04 without secrets. The base text I reviewed (lines 479-1195) shows the release signing, publication and registration docs. These cover the signing key lifetime (keychain deleted before running built files, non-extractable key, notarization credentials scoped to one step), read-only workflow tokens, hash-pinned AWS CLI installs, and source gating via provider-release-resume.py verify-source. They also cover the signing certificate pin list, rollback, and revocation behavior.

Because only docs changed, no runtime control, trust boundary or threat-model assumption (TB-003, TB-009, TB-011, T-013, T-034, T-054) is weakened in the supplied evidence. Concern for the next pass: the real workflow files (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml, scripts/provider-release-resume.py verify-source) are not supplied. I cannot confirm that the scheduled and workflow_dispatch triggers still enforce a dev-ref-only source gate, avoid exposing secrets to an untrusted ref, or keep `secrets: inherit` limited to dev-prefixed secrets. If those workflow changes land in the same PR, they should be reviewed, since the dev-branch build gets the production Developer ID signature and is accepted by self-updater and fan-helper requirements. The truncated patch also hides the new gate description, so that part is unverified. This is a coverage limit, not a finding.
